disconnected.title: Unprotected
disconnected.detail: Your traffic isn't going through the VPN.

lockedDown.title: Blocked by the kill switch

offline.title: No internet connection

auth_required.title: Sign in to connect
auth_required.explanation: This device isn't linked to an account.
auth_required.cause: You signed out, or the device was removed from your account.
auth_required.action: Sign in again; the app re-registers this device.

subscription_inactive.title: Your plan has ended
subscription_inactive.cause: The trial or subscription period is over.
subscription_inactive.action: Choose a plan in Account → Subscription.

no_internet.title: No internet connection
no_internet.explanation: The device isn't connected to a network.
no_internet.cause: Wi-Fi is off, the cable is unplugged, or the network is down.
no_internet.action: Reconnect to a network; the VPN resumes by itself.

server_unavailable.title: Server unavailable
server_unavailable.explanation: The server you chose isn't accepting connections right now.
server_unavailable.cause: Maintenance, an outage, or no servers match your filters.
server_unavailable.action: Pick another location, or let Smart Connect choose.

no_matching_server.title: No server matches
no_matching_server.explanation: No server fits the country, city or features you asked for.
no_matching_server.cause: The combination is too narrow, or those servers were retired.
no_matching_server.action: Loosen the filters or pick another location.

relay_list_unavailable.title: Server list unavailable
relay_list_unavailable.explanation: The app hasn't been able to download the list of servers.
relay_list_unavailable.cause: No internet, or the Meridian service is unreachable.
relay_list_unavailable.action: Check your connection, then try again.

relay_list_invalid.title: Server list rejected
relay_list_invalid.explanation: The downloaded server list failed its signature check and was not used.
relay_list_invalid.cause: The list was altered on the way, possibly by a network interfering with it.
relay_list_invalid.action: Switch networks and try again. If it persists, contact support.

protocol_unavailable.title: Protocol not available
protocol_unavailable.explanation: The selected protocol can't be used with this build or this server.
protocol_unavailable.cause: OpenVPN and IKEv2 aren't included in this build yet.
protocol_unavailable.action: Choose Automatic or WireGuard in Settings → Protocols.

permission_denied.title: Missing permissions
permission_denied.explanation: The VPN service doesn't have the rights it needs.
permission_denied.cause: The service isn't running with system privileges.
permission_denied.action: Reinstall Meridian, or restart the service as administrator.

driver_unavailable.title: Tunnel driver missing
driver_unavailable.explanation: The WireGuard driver couldn't be loaded.
driver_unavailable.cause: The driver file is missing or failed its signature check.

handshake_timeout.title: Server didn't respond
handshake_timeout.explanation: The encrypted handshake with the server timed out.
handshake_timeout.cause: The network may block VPN traffic (UDP), or the server is overloaded.
handshake_timeout.action: Try another server, another network, or Automatic protocol.

tunnel_verification_failed.title: Tunnel isn't passing traffic
tunnel_verification_failed.explanation: The tunnel was set up, but nothing came back through it.
tunnel_verification_failed.cause: A firewall or the network is interfering, or the server has a problem.
tunnel_verification_failed.action: Try another server. Run diagnostics if it keeps happening.

tunnel_failure.title: Connection failed
tunnel_failure.cause: A driver or network problem on this device.
tunnel_failure.action: Try again. Run diagnostics if it keeps happening.

dns_failure.title: DNS couldn't be configured
dns_failure.explanation: The VPN couldn't make Windows use its secure DNS.
dns_failure.cause: Another program is managing DNS on this device.
dns_failure.action: Try again, or choose another DNS option in Settings → DNS.

routing_failure.title: Routing couldn't be configured
routing_failure.explanation: Traffic couldn't be directed into the tunnel.
routing_failure.cause: Another VPN or network tool is changing routes.
routing_failure.action: Close other VPN software and try again.

firewall_failure.title: Kill switch couldn't be enabled
firewall_failure.explanation: The firewall rules couldn't be installed, so Meridian refused to connect without them.
firewall_failure.cause: The service lacks permissions, or another program is holding the firewall.
firewall_failure.action: Run diagnostics. Turning the kill switch off lets you connect without this protection.

configuration_corrupted.title: Settings were reset
configuration_corrupted.explanation: Stored settings were unreadable and have been reset to safe defaults.
configuration_corrupted.action: Review your settings. A copy of the damaged file was kept for support.

unsupported_platform.title: Not supported here yet
unsupported_platform.explanation: This part of Meridian isn't implemented on this operating system yet.
unsupported_platform.cause: macOS and Linux support is in progress.
unsupported_platform.action: Use Meridian on Windows for now.

internal.title: Something went wrong
internal.explanation: An unexpected error occurred in the VPN service.
internal.action: Try again, and send a diagnostics report if it repeats.

overview.intro: What Meridian has verified about this connection, right now. There is no score: each item is either verified, not protected, or can't be verified, and says why.

why.vpnUp: Handshake completed and traffic verified through the tunnel.
why.ipChecked: An external check saw the VPN server's address.
why.ipOwn: An external check saw your own address.
why.ipUnchecked: Run the security check to confirm what the internet sees.
why.dnsOn: Queries go only to the tunnel's resolvers; others are blocked by the firewall.
why.dnsOff: DNS leak protection is off or the system resolver is used.
why.ipv6Tunneled: IPv6 is carried inside the tunnel.
why.ipv6Blocked: IPv6 outside the tunnel is blocked.
why.ksOn: Firewall rules block traffic outside the tunnel.
why.ksOff: The kill switch is off; traffic can leave unprotected while reconnecting.
why.ksUnavailable: The firewall isn't available to the service.
why.wireguard: WireGuard: ChaCha20-Poly1305 with Curve25519 key exchange.
why.ksIdle: Ready: it starts blocking the moment you press Connect. Nothing is being held right now, so there is nothing to verify.

ip.intro: What an external service sees when this device connects to the internet.
ip.geoUnavailable: Location details need a GeoIP database, which this server doesn't have configured.
ip.never: Not checked yet. Run the security check.

leaks.intro: Each test observes your connection now and reports exactly what it saw. When there isn't enough evidence, it says so instead of guessing.
leaks.connectFirst: Connect to run the leak test; with no tunnel there's nothing to test.

details.notConnected: Connect to see the technical details of the tunnel.

findings.not_connected: Not connected, so there's no tunnel to test.
findings.ip_service_unreachable: The IP check service couldn't be reached.
findings.ip_check_not_public: The IP check service is on this machine or network, so it can't see your public address.
findings.exit_is_vpn_server: The internet sees the VPN server's address.
findings.exit_is_your_own_ip: The internet sees your own address. Your IP is not hidden.
findings.exit_differs_from_server: The address seen differs from the server's published address; the server may use a separate exit address.
findings.no_ipv6_check_endpoint: IPv6 goes through the tunnel, but no IPv6 check service is available to confirm the exit address.
findings.no_ipv6_on_network: Your network has no IPv6, so nothing can leak over it.
findings.ipv6_blocked_outside_tunnel: IPv6 outside the tunnel is blocked by verified firewall rules.
findings.firewall_not_verified: IPv6 blocking is configured but the firewall rules couldn't be confirmed.
findings.ipv6_not_blocked: Your network has IPv6 and it isn't blocked outside the tunnel.
findings.system_dns_in_use: "Automatic" DNS is selected, so lookups may go to your network's resolver.
findings.dns_leak_protection_off: DNS leak protection is turned off.
findings.resolver_outside_tunnel_answered: A resolver outside the tunnel answered a query. DNS can leak.
findings.dns_config_unreadable: Windows didn't report the DNS configuration of the tunnel.
findings.dns_config_verified: Only the tunnel's DNS servers are configured and leak blocking is active.
findings.dns_only_via_tunnel: Your network's own resolvers were unreachable (blocked) and only the tunnel's resolvers are configured.
findings.unexpected_tunnel_resolver: An unexpected DNS server is configured on the tunnel.
findings.webrtc_matches_vpn: WebRTC revealed only the VPN's address.
findings.webrtc_exposes_own_ip: WebRTC revealed your own public address.
findings.webrtc_no_candidates: WebRTC couldn't reach a STUN server, so exposure couldn't be checked.
findings.webrtc_unavailable: WebRTC isn't available in this app's browser engine.
findings.webrtc_note: Tested in Meridian's built-in browser engine by contacting a public STUN server (stun.l.google.com). Your web browser may behave differently.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.intro: Checks each part of the connection and explains anything that isn't working.

online.summary: Connected to the internet and the Meridian service.

no_network.causes: Wi-Fi is off, the cable is unplugged, or airplane mode is on.

blocked_by_kill_switch.summary: The kill switch is blocking traffic, which is expected while it holds.
blocked_by_kill_switch.causes: The VPN is reconnecting or failed, and the kill switch is protecting you.

network_up_service_unreachable.summary: The network is up, but Meridian's service can't be reached.
network_up_service_unreachable.causes: A captive portal (hotel, airport), a firewall, or a Meridian outage.
network_up_service_unreachable.actions: Open a browser to complete any sign-in page, then run the checks again.

no_resolvers.causes: The network didn't provide DNS servers.
no_resolvers.actions: Reconnect to the network, or set custom DNS in Settings → DNS.

resolvers_not_answering.causes: The resolver is down, or the network blocks DNS.
resolvers_not_answering.actions: Try custom DNS, or another network.

some_resolvers_failing.actions: Usually harmless; the others take over.

running.summary: The service is running with everything it needs.

tunnel_driver_missing.causes: The driver file is missing or failed its signature check.

firewall_unavailable.summary: The service can't use the firewall, so the kill switch can't work.
firewall_unavailable.causes: The service isn't running with system privileges.
firewall_unavailable.actions: Reinstall Meridian or start the service as administrator.

reachable.summary: Servers are reachable from this device.

servers_unreachable.causes: The network blocks ICMP or VPN traffic, or there's an outage.
servers_unreachable.actions: Try another network. If others work, contact support.

server_list_stale.summary: Servers answer, but the server list is out of date.
server_list_stale.causes: The list couldn't be refreshed recently.
server_list_stale.actions: It refreshes on its own when the service is reachable.

handshake_fresh.summary: The tunnel handshake is recent and healthy.

handshake_stale.summary: The server hasn't completed a handshake recently.
handshake_stale.causes: The server stopped responding or the network is interfering.

no_handshake.causes: UDP may be blocked on this network.

default_route_via_tunnel.summary: Internet traffic is routed through the tunnel.

default_route_bypasses_tunnel.summary: Traffic is not routed through the tunnel.
default_route_bypasses_tunnel.causes: Another VPN or network tool changed the routes.
default_route_bypasses_tunnel.actions: Close other VPN software and reconnect.

route_unknown.actions: Reconnect and run the checks again.

active.summary: The kill switch rules are installed and verified.

kill_switch_off.causes: It was turned off in settings.
kill_switch_off.actions: Turn it on in Settings → Kill switch to avoid exposure while reconnecting.

rules_not_as_expected.summary: The firewall rules don't match what Meridian installed.
rules_not_as_expected.causes: Another program changed the firewall, or applying rules failed.
rules_not_as_expected.actions: Reconnect. If it persists, restart the computer.

no_ipv6_on_network.summary: Your network has no IPv6, so there's nothing to leak.

ipv6_blocked_outside_tunnel.summary: IPv6 is blocked outside the tunnel.

ipv6_may_leak.actions: Turn on "Block IPv6 leaks" in Settings → Network.

not_connected.summary: Not connected, so this check doesn't apply.

signed_in.summary: Signed in, and this device is registered.

signed_out.causes: You signed out or the session expired.

device_not_registered.summary: This device isn't registered with your account.
device_not_registered.causes: It was removed, or registration didn't finish.
device_not_registered.actions: Sign in again to register it.

subscription_inactive.causes: The trial or subscription has ended.
subscription_inactive.actions: Choose a plan in Account → Subscription.

api_unreachable.summary: Meridian's account service can't be reached.
api_unreachable.causes: No internet or a network blocking it.
api_unreachable.actions: Check the connection and try again.

service_unreachable.summary: The VPN service isn't running or can't be reached.
service_unreachable.causes: It was stopped, crashed, or isn't installed correctly.
service_unreachable.actions: Restart the computer. If that doesn't help, reinstall Meridian.

protocols.intro: The protocol is how your device and the server build the encrypted tunnel. Automatic picks the best available one for your network.

automatic.name: Automatic
automatic.desc: Uses WireGuard, and would switch to a TCP-based protocol on networks that block UDP once one is available in this build.

wireguard.name: WireGuard
wireguard.desc: Modern, minimal and fast, running in the Windows kernel.
wireguard.pros: Fastest; quick to connect and reconnect; small, audited codebase; strong modern cryptography.
wireguard.cons: UDP only, so some restrictive networks block it.

openvpn.name: OpenVPN
openvpn.desc: Mature and widely supported, and can run over TCP port 443.
openvpn.pros: Gets through restrictive firewalls over TCP; long track record.
openvpn.cons: Slower than WireGuard; slower to connect.
openvpn.compatibility: Excellent, including networks that block UDP

ikev2.name: IKEv2/IPsec
ikev2.desc: Built into operating systems and quick to re-establish on network changes.

killSwitch.intro: The kill switch uses the Windows firewall to stop your traffic from leaving this device outside the VPN.

off.name: Off
off.desc: No blocking. While connecting or reconnecting, your traffic can briefly go out unprotected.

while_connected.name: On while connected
while_connected.desc: From the moment you press Connect until you disconnect, nothing leaves outside the tunnel, including during reconnects and errors.

always_on.name: Always on
always_on.desc: Nothing leaves outside the tunnel, ever, even when disconnected and from system startup. You'll have no internet until you connect.

killSwitch.blocked: What's blocked: every connection that doesn't go through the tunnel.
killSwitch.allowed: Still allowed: this computer talking to itself, getting a network address (DHCP), the VPN server itself, signing in to your Meridian account, and your local network if you allow it below.
killSwitch.allowLanDesc: Printers, casting and file shares on your home network keep working.
killSwitch.offConfirmBody: Without it, your real IP address can be exposed for a few seconds every time the VPN reconnects.
killSwitch.alwaysOnConfirmBody: With Always on, this device has no internet access at all unless the VPN is connected, including right after startup.

dns.intro: DNS turns names like example.com into addresses. Whoever answers those lookups can see which sites you visit.

vpn.name: VPN DNS
vpn.desc: Meridian's resolver on the VPN server, reached through the tunnel. Recommended.

custom.name: Custom DNS
custom.desc: Resolvers you choose, reached through the tunnel.

system.name: Automatic (your network's DNS)
system.desc: Leaves DNS alone. Your network provider may see the sites you visit.

dns.invalidIp: That isn't a valid IP address.
dns.blockLeaksDesc: While connected, blocks DNS queries to any resolver other than the one Meridian uses.
dns.dohNote: Encrypted DNS in web browsers (DNS over HTTPS) looks like normal web traffic and can't be blocked by port. It still travels inside the tunnel.
dns.statusDisconnected: Your network's DNS ({{servers}}); the VPN isn't connected
dns.leakRisk: May reveal sites to your network

network.intro: Most people never need to change these.
network.ipv6: Use IPv6 through the VPN when available
network.ipv6Desc: Carries IPv6 inside the tunnel when the server supports it.
network.blockIpv6Desc: When the tunnel carries only IPv4, IPv6 outside the tunnel is blocked.
network.allowLanDesc: Reach printers, NAS and other devices at home while connected.
network.mtuDesc: Largest packet size in the tunnel. Automatic works for almost everyone; lower it only if some sites load partially.
network.mtuWarningBody: A wrong value can make some websites stall or fail. Automatic (1420) is right for almost every network.
network.keepaliveDesc: Keeps the connection alive through home routers and NAT. Seconds; 0 turns it off.
network.natDesc: Your device shares the VPN server's public address with other users (NAT). No inbound connections reach you through the VPN.

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.body: Press Connect on the dashboard. Meridian picks the best server for you (Smart Connect). To choose a place yourself, open Servers and pick a country or city. "Protected" appears only once the tunnel is up and verified.

kill-switch.title: What the kill switch does
kill-switch.body: The kill switch uses the Windows firewall so nothing leaves your device outside the VPN. "On while connected" protects you from pressing Connect until you disconnect, including every reconnect. "Always on" also blocks everything while you're disconnected.

dns-leaks.title: DNS leaks, explained
dns-leaks.body: Every site you open starts with a DNS lookup. If those lookups go to your provider instead of through the VPN, they reveal where you're going. Meridian sends lookups through the tunnel and blocks any that try to go elsewhere.

split-tunneling.title: Split tunneling
split-tunneling.body: Split tunneling lets some apps bypass the VPN. On Windows it needs a network driver that isn't in this build yet; until then, your rules are saved and all traffic stays in the VPN.

trusted-networks.title: Trusted networks and auto-connect
trusted-networks.body: Add networks you know (home, work) and choose what Meridian does on them. On any other network, it can connect automatically. Open Wi-Fi is treated as untrusted.

privacy.title: What we log (and don't)
privacy.body: We never record your traffic, the sites you visit, or your DNS queries. We store your account email, plan and devices. See Settings → Privacy for every category.

faq.q1: Why does the app say "Unable to verify"?
faq.a1: Some checks need evidence that isn't available, for example an external IPv6 test server. Meridian says so instead of guessing.
faq.q2: Why is latency "—" for some servers?
faq.a2: Latency is measured from your device. Servers that haven't been measured yet, or didn't answer, show "—" rather than an estimate.
faq.a3: Not in this build. WireGuard is used, and Automatic will be able to fall back to OpenVPN once it's added.
faq.q4: How many devices can I use?
faq.a4: The trial allows 2 devices, paid plans 10. Manage them in Account → Devices.
faq.q5: I have no internet after closing Meridian.
faq.a5: Your kill switch is probably set to Always on, or the VPN was still meant to be connected. Open Meridian and disconnect, or change the kill switch mode.

troubleshooting.intro: Pick what's happening; each guide runs the relevant checks.

cantConnect.title: I can't connect
cantConnect.body: Usually the network blocks VPN traffic or the server is busy. Run the checks, then try another server.

slow.title: The connection is slow
slow.body: Choose a closer or less busy server (Servers → sort by Latency or Load). Speed depends on distance and your own connection.

noInternet.title: Connected, but no internet
noInternet.body: Run the checks. DNS or routing problems show up there with steps to fix them.

sitesBlock.title: A site blocks me on VPN
sitesBlock.body: Try another server, or a server with the Streaming feature for video services.

contact.intro: Tell us what's wrong. We usually reply within a day.
contact.subject: Subject
contact.descriptionHint: What happened, when, and what you were trying to do.
contact.attachHint: Up to 5 files, 10 MB each (PNG, JPEG, TXT, JSON, ZIP, PDF).
contact.includeReportHint: Contains check results and versions, with IP addresses masked. Preview it before sending.
contact.sent: Request #{{number}} sent. We'll reply by email.
contact.signInRequired: Sign in to contact support from the app.

welcome.title: Welcome to Meridian
welcome.body: A VPN that encrypts your connection and hides your IP address, and is honest about exactly what it protects.

privacy.title: Your privacy, plainly
privacy.body: We never log your traffic, the sites you visit or your DNS queries. This build sends no analytics. Diagnostics reports are sent only when you choose to.

how.title: How it works
how.body: A small background service builds an encrypted WireGuard tunnel to a server of your choice. The service needs system permissions to create the tunnel and firewall rules; the installer set that up.
how.serviceMissing: Not reachable. Reinstall or start the service.

protection.title: Protection defaults
protection.body: These are on by default. You can change them later in Settings.

autoConnect.title: Connect automatically?
autoConnect.body: Meridian can connect on untrusted networks like cafés and airports.

account.title: Sign in
account.body: Sign in or create an account to connect this device.

connect.title: You're all set
connect.body: Smart Connect picks the best server for you. Press Connect when you're ready.

empty.title: You're all caught up
empty.body: Connection changes, security alerts and account news show up here.

osNotify.disconnected: Disconnected. Your traffic isn't going through the VPN.
osNotify.killSwitch: The kill switch is blocking traffic until the VPN reconnects.
